newsitem.title: SYRIA: Egypt's Mubarak meets Assad in Syria.
newsitem.headline: Egypt's Mubarak meets Assad in Syria.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak held talks with Syrian President Hafez al-Assad in Damascus on Tuesday on Middle East peace developments and bilateral ties.
Presidential spokesman Joubran Kourieh said Assad greeted the Egyptian leader at Damascus airport when he arrived in the afternoon on a previously unannounced visit.
Officials said the talks would focus on the deadlocked Syrian-Israeli peace talks and Israeli settlements in the occupied Arab lands.

No talks have been held between Syria and Israel since Benjamin Netanyahu became prime minister in June last year because of his refusal to swap occupied Arab lands for peace, a principle on which the peace talks were based when they were started in 1991.
Syria wants Israel to accept full withdrawal from the Golan Heights, captured by Israel in 1967, before resuming peace talks.
Kourieh said Mubarak was joined at the talks by Egyptian Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri, Foreign Minister Amr Moussa, Information Minister Safwat el-Sherif and other ministers.
Present from the Syrian side were Vice-President Abdel-Halim Khaddam, Prime Minister Mahmoud Zu'bi and Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara.
Kourieh said the two presidents later held a private meeting.

Mubarak's trip to Syria took place a day after Israel put the brakes on a plan to build a new Jewish enclave in Arab East Jerusalem and agreed to resume talks with the PLO on meeting commitments made under their interim peace deals.

Israel's interior ministry suspended a permit granted to a U.S. Jewish land baron to build 70 Jewish homes in an Arab neighbourhood until an appeal by two left-wing Jerusalem city council members had been heard.
Tuesday's edition of the Egyptian government daily al-Ahram newspaper said Mubarak sent a message Netanyahu on Monday warning of the dangers to peace if Israel allowed the settlement to be built.
Egypt in 1979 became the first Arab country to sign a peace treaty with Israel and has often mediated in peace talks between the Jewish state and its Arab neighbours.
